text:
Maya R.: Quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing we split the view-assembly API into two strata: a 'planner' (composition) layer and a 'renderer' (materialization) layer. Planner does graph planning, auth dedupe, tenant scoping; renderer does tile materialization, caching, and render-time perf. Main goals: reduce auth fanout, shrink cache working sets, and simplify per-stripe SLOs. Thoughts?

Sam C.: Love the idea. Can you quantify expected p95 gains and what extra RPCs this adds?

Maya R.: Short answer: for dashboards with many panels auth on each panel is the biggest multiplier. Planner can dedupe auth and emit a single permission set + compact plan. Sim: 40-panel dashboard -> 40 auth calls -> planner reduces to 1 auth call, plus batched planner->renderer requests. p95 improvement ~20-30% in our synthetic runs. Extra RPCs are batched plan shipments, not per-panel RPCs if we design the plan shape thoughtfully.

Oliver K.: Main concern is hop+serialization cost. If planner and renderer are separate services we may add a hop per render unless we batch/stream. We should measure serialization overhead for the plan vs current payload.

Priya S.: Suggest colocating renderer with the serving runtime (close to GPU/worker nodes) for low-latency materialization. Planner can live in a control-plane tier. Also need to keep per-panel feature flags and A/B assignment in the planner output.

Maya R.: Agreed. Implementation sketch: planner returns a compact plan schema that describes nodes, deps, cache hints. Renderer receives plan + short-lived token to perform materialization. Example plan (sketch):
```
{
  "plan_version": "v1",
  "tenant_id": "T123",
  "nodes": [
    {"id":"n1", "type":"query", "source":"metrics", "args":{"span":"5m"}},
    {"id":"n2", "type":"transform", "deps":["n1"]}
  ],
  "cache_hints":{"n1":"ttl=30s","n2":"no-cache"}
}
```

Ben D.: Strong versioning and rollback story required. Make plan_version required and allow renderer to reject unknown versions. Canary by tenant hash and percent rollout is how we should stage. For RBAC: planner must compute and assert the final permission surface so renderer can be 'dumb' about auth.

Sam C.: Failure modes? If renderer misbehaves, we need a fallback to the legacy path or degrade gracefully. Also need to consider partial renders (some tiles fail).

Maya R.: Yes — plan includes an optional 'legacy_payload' or 'legacy_fallback' flag. Rollout checklist: canary by tenant, percent increase, latency and error rate gates, automatic rollback on error spike. Also add an operator override to pin tenants to legacy.

Oliver K.: +1 on streaming/batching RPCs. Recommend gRPC multiplexed streams for planner->renderer so renderer can start materializing as plan arrives and we can pipe partial results. That reduces tail latency.

Priya S.: Telemetry counters to add: plan_size_bytes, plan_nodes, render_time_ms, cache_hit, auth_dedupe_count, fallback_rate. That will help validate benefits.

Maya R.: Great. I'll open an RFC/PR with API sketches, migration playbook, and perf test harness. @Ben D. @Oliver K. can you help with the versioning spec and perf harness? :thumbsup:

infra-bot: maya_r pushed branch maya/view-assembly-strata -> opened PR #2478

Sam C.: Ack, will review once the PR lands.
